sparql:
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX dc: <http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/>
PREFIX event: <http://purl.org/NET/c4dm/event.owl#>
PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
PREFIX tl: <http://purl.org/NET/c4dm/timeline.owl#>
SELECT ?releaseEvent 
 WHERE {
 ?releaseEvent rdf:type mo:ReleaseEvent .
 ?releaseEvent dc:title "%s" .
 ?releaseEvent event:time ?date .
 ?date rdf:type tl:Instant .
 ?date tl:at "%s" .
 }
gold_question: Which release event with the given title occurred at the specified date/time?

review.note: The wording is fine but the concept of ReleaseEvent is not very NL friendly. It is probably used here to find the label that released the album. But on its own, this query does not make much sense to anyone not intimately familiar witht he ontology

model_output.nl_question: Which release event with the given title occurred at the specified date/time?
model_output.confidence_rationale: No provided evidence directly matches a query about a release event filtered by title and exact time. The question is generated from the SPARQL, which selects a mo:ReleaseEvent with a given dc:title occurring at a specified tl:Instant.

sparql:
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX dc: <http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/>
PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
SELECT ?medium 
 WHERE {
 ?medium rdf:type mo:Record .
 ?medium dc:title "%s" .
 ?medium mo:record_number "%i" .
 }
gold_question: Which record has the given title and record number?

review.note: This one is looking for a specific disk within a larger release (usually a large compilation), by the disk title and number. The model would not be able to know it without knowing more about the ontology. The generated NL is not wrong, it just misses the context

model_output.nl_question: Which record has the given title and record number?
model_output.confidence_rationale: No provided evidence aligns with this lookup-style query. The SPARQL clearly filters mo:Record by dc:title and mo:record_number and returns the matching record, so the generated question closely reflects the query’s intent.

sparql:
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX dtl: <http://www.DTL.org/schema/properties/>
PREFIX event: <http://purl.org/NET/c4dm/event.owl#>
PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
SELECT DISTINCT ?artist 
 WHERE {
 ?artist rdf:type mo:MusicArtist .
 ?artist foaf:name "%s" .
 ?performer dtl:musician ?artist .
 ?performance mo:performer ?performer .
 ?session event:sub_event ?performance .
 ?session mo:performer <%s> .
 }
gold_question: Find the musician by name who played in a session with the given performer

review.note: This seems to be a disambiguation query rather then search, since we already have the name. I would dismiss it

model_output.nl_question: Which artist with the given name performed in the same recording session as the given performer?
model_output.confidence_rationale: No suitable NL evidence directly matches this query, so the question is generated from the SPARQL structure. The pattern clearly identifies an artist by name who participated in a session that also included the given performer, but absence of aligned evidence lowers confidence.
